versions.request: Renovate or upgrade an existing health care facility
versions.explanation: South Brooklyn Health Hospital (at 2601 Ocean Parkway) is the closest hospital to our community district, located on Ocean Parkway and near the Belt Parkway. South Brookly Health Hospital needs additional funding to become a Level 1 Trauma Center. They currently do not have the equipment needed to designate them as such. Brooklyn Community Board 15 would like to see them properly funded to be eligible for this important trauma care designation.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency does not support and cannot accommodate Explanation: While the cost associated with a Level I Trauma Center is prohibitive at this time due to the requirement of 24/7 trauma surgery and anesthesia coverage, South Brooklyn Health is able to care for hundreds of traumatically injured patients per year in its fully prepared resuscitation rooms. The hospital has a trauma response team on standby for any incoming codes and performs multiple drills to be ready for patients that are brought in for care. In addition, the hospital recently appointed an EMS and Disaster Fellowship trained Director for Trauma and Prehospital Medicine to ensure preparedness and quality. The new 11-story tower building includes a new elevated Emergency Department, state of the art operating rooms including robotic surgery, single bedded inpatient beds, a number of modern specialty care endoscopy and interventional radiology and cardiology services, new entrances from Ocean Parkway, a new flood wall, improved parking for patients and staff, and much more. The redevelopment is part of a major $922.7 million hospital campus renovation funded by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to demolish, replace and repair flood damaged buildings from Superstorm Sandy.

versions.request: Forestry services, including street tree maintenance
versions.explanation: Brooklyn Community Board 15 receives numerous complaints about trees not being pruned, maintained or planted in a timely fashion. More money needs to be allocated to provide better forestry services to our community. New trees should be planted within two-three planting cycles; waiting 4 or 5 years is a ridiculously long time. Tree pruning can take 7-10 years, allowing overgrown and dead branches to become a public safety hazard. We need to expedite this process. Adequately funding this division with additional trained staff and equipment would streamline this vital function.
versions.response: The agency has stated that they will try to accommodate this request with existing resources. OMB supports this.

versions.request: Other commercial district revitalization requests
versions.explanation: We have a large number of small commercial corridors in our district (i.e.; Avenue U, Sheepshead Bay Road, Avenue P, Gravesend Neck Road and Avenue X) with rents sky-rocketing to ludicrous heights. These storefronts either turnover rapidly, or sit vacant warehoused without attracting new businesses or new investment in the community. Empty storefronts don't entice consumers. They reduce foot traffic to the corridors. Things have gone from bad to worse. The City needs to offer indepedent small business owners more incentives and assistance in creating businesses, or offer property owners some incentives to attract and retain businesses. Outrageous rents are keeping many of our small commercial areas bleak and depressed.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: SBS has made investments in commercial corridors in the district through a variety of grants. SBS has supported local commercial revitalization through the Kings Highway BID, which received Small BID Grants this Fiscal Year and in FY24 and a Commercial District Lighting grant in FY24. This Fiscal Year, SBS also provided the Brooklyn Alliance, who previously deployed select interventions along the commercial corridors in the district through an Avenue NYC grant SBS provided, a Merchant Organizing grant to support commercial districts and merchant organizing in the community. SBS will continue to promote grant programs when available and encourage the community boards to share information about our grant programs with local non-profits. While commercial rents are set by private commercial property-owners and the city does not have an ability to regulate commercial rents, SBS is proud to deliver up to 40 hours of pro-bono Commercial Lease Assistance Program. This service provides businesses legal representation as they negotiate commercial leases and rents with landlords either at the point of signing a new lease, renewing a lease, or supporting pre-litigation issues.

versions.request: Add NYPD parking facilities
versions.explanation: Currently, Brooklyn has only one police Tow Pound in Northern Brooklyn and it's often at full capacity. This is a growing problem for our community. Additional car lifts (stackers) at the existing Tow Pound would increase holding capacity and permit more vehicles to be stored as an immediate interim measure. The current pound being located across the borough results in long travel times. It limits the turnaround time resulting in diminished productivity per work shift for Row Tow operators serving Southern Brooklyn. Ideally, we would like the short-term addition of car lifts at the existing Tow Pound until a new pound can be sited and constructed in Southern Brooklyn to expedite Row Tow operations enhancing their capacity and increasing their productivity.
versions.response: The Administration is currently reviewing this practice

versions.request: Hire additional crossing guards
versions.explanation: All of the schools in our community district would benefit from additional crossing guards. With the severe traffic around many of our schools particularly at dismissal times, crossing guards provide an essential service to ensure the safety of our students and community members as they navigate these congested and often chaotic public spaces. Currently, when a crossing guard is out sick, a uniformed officer is pulled away to take their place, taking an officer away from other critical policing work. Having additional crossing guards available would provide enhanced coverage at schools without having to draw from our uniformed forces when replacements are needed.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as indicated. Additionally, please note that School Safety Agents are not capital eligible and must be funded with expense.

versions.request: Other NYPD programs requests
versions.explanation: Currently, Explorers must pay a fee of $24 a year to participate in this worthwhile Police program. Ideally, we would like to see that fee paid for or waived by the City of New York to encourage greater participation in the program. We would like to also see the expense of their uniforms covered. We would like to see PAL and other youth programs offered by the NYPD fully funded to get our children off the streets and into safe, learning and nurturing environments. They are our future. We need to get them on the right path.
versions.response: More information is needed from the community board before making a funding decision. The community board should contact the agency.
